thread:
alex: seeing p95 jump ~4x in prod for model-redwood-v2 on pool-eu-west around 09:12 UTC. graphs show KV cache eviction spike + tombstone explosion.

alex: quick metric cut: `evictions/sec: 120 -> 900`, `tombstones: 5k -> 62k`, queue depth climbing on shard-7.

maria: ack, paging eng-runtime oncall. tagging SRE.

sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-0423_kvcache_surge (sev2) — responders: eng-runtime, oncall.

jia: looking — profiler attached. initial guess: kernel selector started favoring fast-attn shortseq path which increases KV churn (more short-lived KV keys). running flameprof + kernel selection trace now.

kevin: can we route traffic off pool-eu-west to pool-eu-central as a quick fallback? adds ~8-12ms but should relieve eviction pressure.

alex: prefer to flip a conservative kernel flag first to avoid cross-region routing churn. propose ff/kernel_fastshort = false.

maria: will flip in 60s and canary at 5%. prepping rollout.

maria: ff/kernel_fastshort=false -> canary 5% :white_check_mark:

alex: canary p95 trending down. good signal. but one tenant still producing high eviction tail (tenant=media-corps). want per-tenant mitigations.

jia: agreed. also perf counters show kernel-selection misfires ++ and batch coalescing windows causing simultaneous cache updates. flameprof shows kernel switch cost ~0.9ms on average for these sequences.

kevin: plan: 1) route media-corps to fallback-cpu-v1 (lower perf but reduces KV churn), 2) set tenant concurrency limit, 3) keep kernel flag off. I can push routing change.

alex: also shrink batch window on pool-eu-west from 10ms -> 4ms as temporary measure to reduce collision surface. will cost throughput but lower p99 risk.

kevin: executing route command: `route set tenant media-corps -> fallback-cpu-v1 weight 0.0->0.6` (canary 20% first).

deploy-bot: deploy job #deploy-4821 started for routing change.

maria: canary routing 20% -> observing.

maria: applying tenant concurrency limit: `set tenant media-corps concurrency_limit=8` -> applied :white_check_mark:

jia: on the canary: batch-window shrink shows ~40% reduction in kernel misfires and eviction spikes. good short-term.

alex: metrics update after 10m: `evictions/sec` down 900 -> 220, `tombstones` down 62k -> 11k, p95 nearly back to normal baseline.

sre-bot: incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. keeping incident open for 60m for observation.

jia: root-cause hypothesis: recent kernel selection heuristic change (fastshort) + binpack change that colocated a noisy tenant increased KV churn and exposed tombstone amplification. kernel heuristic caused more short-lived KV keys and more eviction pressure.

maria: immediate mitigations: kernel_fastshort flag reverted, per-tenant concurrency limit applied, routing for media-corps to fallback-cpu-v1, batch-window reduced on pool-eu-west.

maria: longer-term follow-ups: rollback the kernel heuristic in next release, add per-tenant KV cache quota & tombstone alert, implement hot-tenant auto-shedding, and add synthetic regression tests for kernel selection churn.

alex: I'll open an RFC with profiling attachment and synthetic workload plan: /link/internal/rfc/kernel-heuristic-regression (will include flameprof samples + perf counters).

kevin: thanks all — nice rapid coordination. :thumbsup:

maria: closing out ops actions. I will post the incident summary to #incidents once we confirm 60m stable.

alex: noted. leaving postmortem + action items to RFC. good job team.
